heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: ## Termination for convenience
blocks.plain_text: Termination for convenience

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: Canada may terminate a contract for convenience in accordance with the termination for convenience provision of the general conditions applicable to the contract.
blocks.plain_text: Canada may terminate a contract for convenience in accordance with the termination for convenience provision of the general conditions applicable to the contract.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: You may terminate a contract for the convenience of Canada if:
blocks.plain_text: You may terminate a contract for the convenience of Canada if:

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown:
- the funding has been curtailed
- a government program has been discontinued
- a contract has been mistakenly awarded to other than the lowest responsive offeror
- other circumstances make the procurement of the good or service unnecessary
blocks.plain_text: the funding has been curtailed ; a government program has been discontinued ; a contract has been mistakenly awarded to other than the lowest responsive offeror ; other circumstances make the procurement of the good or service unnecessary

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: Termination for convenience also applies when:
blocks.plain_text: Termination for convenience also applies when:

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown:
- the client has requested termination
- a termination for default cannot be considered because the contractor is not in default
- a termination by mutual consent would not be more advantageous to Canada
blocks.plain_text: the client has requested termination ; a termination for default cannot be considered because the contractor is not in default ; a termination by mutual consent would not be more advantageous to Canada

blocks.plain_text: Termination claims officer

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: The Price Support Directorate (PSD), Procurement Business Management Sector (PBMS) was designated to provide termination settlement services including the processing of claims associated with goods and services contracts terminated for convenience by Canada.
blocks.plain_text: The Price Support Directorate (PSD), Procurement Business Management Sector (PBMS) was designated to provide termination settlement services including the processing of claims associated with goods and services contracts terminated for convenience by Canada.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: When a contract will be terminated for convenience in whole or in part, the PSPC buyer should involve the termination claims officer (TCO), PSD , PBMS immediately in the claim settlement process.
blocks.plain_text: When a contract will be terminated for convenience in whole or in part, the PSPC buyer should involve the termination claims officer (TCO), PSD , PBMS immediately in the claim settlement process.

- issuing stop work orders and notices of termination
- administering the non-terminated portion of the contract

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: ### Preparing for contract termination
blocks.plain_text: Preparing for contract termination

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: Occasionally, the client will require a contract status report before making a decision to cancel the contract. They will inform PSPC of their intention to reduce or cancel a contract by issuing a "notice of intent to cancel" to you. The client may request all or part of the following contract status information before making a final decision to terminate. This report includes:
blocks.plain_text: Occasionally, the client will require a contract status report before making a decision to cancel the contract. They will inform PSPC of their intention to reduce or cancel a contract by issuing a "notice of intent to cancel" to you. The client may request all or part of the following contract status information before making a final decision to terminate. This report includes:

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown:
- the quantity of stores produced during the contract
- the quantity of stores in production
- the value of raw materials or components acquired by the contractor to carry out the specific contract
- the position with respect to tooling and capital equipment, especially if the contractor had to tool-up to carry out the contract
- the status of subcontracts
- the most economical point to terminate the contract
- the approximate amount of termination claims, if known

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: You must immediately request the information from the contractor and provide it to the client along with any recommendations.
blocks.plain_text: You must immediately request the information from the contractor and provide it to the client along with any recommendations.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: Normally, the client's initial request will be to cancel all or part of the contract, in which case you should immediately issue a stop work order. A stop work order is a safeguard to ensure a halt in the work and remove the possibility of further expense being generated by the contractor. To terminate the contract, a stop work order must be followed by issuing a notice of termination for convenience.
blocks.plain_text: Normally, the client's initial request will be to cancel all or part of the contract, in which case you should immediately issue a stop work order. To terminate the contract, a stop work order must be followed by issuing a notice of termination for convenience.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: #### Notice of termination
blocks.plain_text: Notice of termination

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: It is the client's responsibility to decide at what stage a full or partial termination should take place. You must not issue a notice of termination to the contractor until legal opinion is sought and the client’s formal requisition amendment confirming their decision to terminate has been received. In order to avoid further costs to Canada and hardship to the contractor, a notice of termination must be issued as quickly as possible to finalize the implications of the stop work order.
blocks.plain_text: It is the client's responsibility to decide at what stage a full or partial termination should take place. You must not issue a notice of termination to the contractor until legal opinion is sought and the client’s formal requisition amendment confirming their decision to terminate has been received. In order to avoid further costs to Canada and hardship to the contractor, a notice of termination must be issued as quickly as possible to finalize the implications of the stop work order.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: You should ensure that sufficient funds remain in the amended requisition to cover the contract value. You must not adjust the funds when issuing the notice of termination. The contract funds will be adjusted on the settlement and release document.
blocks.plain_text: You should ensure that sufficient funds remain in the amended requisition to cover the contract value. You must not adjust the funds when issuing the notice of termination. The contract funds will be adjusted on the settlement and release document.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: You will prepare the notice of termination or partial termination using the appropriate contract clauses and based on advice from Legal Services, send the notice of termination to the contractor.
blocks.plain_text: You will prepare the notice of termination or partial termination using the appropriate contract clauses and based on advice from Legal Services, send the notice of termination to the contractor.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: After the notice of termination or partial termination is issued, you must immediately send a copy of the stop work order and notice of termination to the TCO .
blocks.plain_text: After the notice of termination or partial termination is issued, you must immediately send a copy of the stop work order and notice of termination to the TCO .

blocks.markdown: If the contractor advises you that a claim will not be submitted following the receipt of a notice of termination, you must remove the funding for the terminated items. Since no claim is made, the TCO is not part of this process.

blocks.plain_text: Audit of claims

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
blocks.markdown: Upon receipt of a claim, the TCO will determine the need for an audit. If required, they will prepare the terms of reference and arrange for its completion. The TCO will also review the cost factors reported by the auditor and reconcile the contractor's claim with the auditor's report. The cost implications of any inventory adjustments should be discussed with the auditor and the contractor.

blocks.markdown: Price Support Directorate (PSD), Procurement Business Management Sector (PBMS) is designated to handle claims arising from United States and Canadian Commercial Corporation (U.S./CCC) contracts being terminated for the convenience of the U.S. government.
blocks.plain_text: Price Support Directorate (PSD), Procurement Business Management Sector (PBMS) is designated to handle claims arising from United States and Canadian Commercial Corporation (U.S./CCC) contracts being terminated for the convenience of the U.S. government.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Terminate or suspend a contract - Termination for convenience
Claims arising from United States and Canadian Commercial Corporation contracts
blocks.markdown: For terminations involving U.S./CCC contracts, the executive director, Strategic Policy Development and Integration Directorate (SPDID), Strategic Policy Sector (SPS), will ensure compliance with the certification and termination settlement functions that are required to conform with the U.S. Department of Defense and Department of National Defence Letter of Agreement (see U.S. Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplements 225.870-6 and 249.7000 ).

blocks.markdown: The executive director, SPDID will also respond to requests from the U.S. government to arrange audits of U.S. government contracts or subcontracts placed directly with Canadian-based suppliers that are terminated for convenience.
